content: 1. Gentamicin can decrease renal clearance of certain drugs, but the clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. This interaction is primarily observed in preterm infants. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Atenolol increases serum potassium levels, while gentamicin decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is not well understood, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 3. Gentamicin enhances the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 4. Aztreonam and gentamicin may increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination can be used synergistically against Pseudomonas spp. and Enterobacteriaceae, but the clinical significance is uncertain. 5. Gentamicin and bacitracin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Concurrent use should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 6. Gentamicin decreases the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 7. Gentamicin decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Gentamicin decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine live through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Administration of live bacterial vaccines should be delayed until antibiotic therapy is completed. 9. Bendroflumethiazide and gentamicin both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 10. Betaxolol increases serum potassium levels, while gentamicin decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Gentamicin decreases the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 12. Bisoprolol increases serum potassium levels, while gentamicin decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Bumetanide and gentamicin both decrease serum potassium levels. Additionally, either drug can increase the toxicity of the other through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 14. Gentamicin decreases the levels of calcium acetate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 15. Gentamicin decreases the levels of calcium carbonate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 16. Gentamicin decreases the levels of calcium chloride by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 17. Gentamicin decreases the levels of calcium citrate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 18. Gentamicin decreases the levels of calcium gluconate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 19. Candesartan increases serum potassium levels, while gentamicin decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Capreomycin and gentamicin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 21. Carbenoxolone and gentamicin both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 22. Carboplatin and gentamicin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 23. Carvedilol increases serum potassium levels, while gentamicin decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Cephalosporins, such as cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefditoren, cefepime, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefotetan, cefoxitin, cefpirome, cefpodoxime, cefprozil, ceftaroline, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, ceftizoxime, ceftobiprole, ceftolozane/tazobactam, ceftriaxone, and cefuroxime, can increase the nephrotoxic effects of gentamicin. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 25. Celecoxib increases serum potassium levels, while gentamicin decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Celecoxib may also increase gentamicin levels by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is primarily observed in preterm infants, and its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 27. Celiprolol increases serum potassium levels, while gentamicin decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Chlorothiazide and gentamicin both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 29. Chlorthalidone and gentamicin both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 30. Gentamicin and the cholera vaccine exhibit pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration of the cholera vaccine with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may be active against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 31. Choline magnesium trisalicylate increases serum potassium levels, while gentamicin decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Choline magnesium trisalicylate may also increase gentamicin levels by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is primarily observed in preterm infants, and its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 33. Cidofovir and gentamicin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 34. Gentamicin enhances the effects of cisatracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 35. Cisplatin and gentamicin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 36. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of gentamicin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 37. Clotrimazole decreases the levels or effects of gentamicin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 38. Colistin and gentamicin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 39. Gentamicin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Contrast media (iodinated) and gentamicin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 41. Cordyceps may decrease the toxicity of gentamicin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 42. Gentamicin decreases the levels of cyanocobalamin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 43. Cyclopenthiazide and gentamicin both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 44. Cyclosporine and gentamicin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 45. Cytarabine decreases the effects of gentamicin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 46. Gentamicin enhances the effects of daxibotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 47. Deferasirox and gentamicin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity. Acute renal failure has been reported with deferasirox. Coadministration with nephrotoxic drugs, including aminoglycosides, may increase this risk. Monitor serum creatinine and/or creatinine clearance in patients receiving both agents. 48. Gentamicin and deflazacort both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 49. Dichlorphenamide and gentamicin both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 50. Diclofenac increases serum potassium levels, while gentamicin decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 51. Diclofenac may also increase gentamicin levels by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is primarily observed in preterm infants, and its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 52. Gentamicin decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. An alternative or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 53. Diflunisal increases serum potassium levels, while gentamicin decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 54. Diflunisal may also increase gentamicin levels by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is primarily observed in preterm infants, and its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 55. Gentamicin increases the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Additionally, digoxin increases serum potassium levels, while gentamicin decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 56. Dobutamine and gentamicin both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 57. Dopamine and gentamicin both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 58. Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of gentamicin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 59. Drospirenone increases serum potassium levels, while gentamicin decreases them. The clinical effect of this interaction is unclear, so therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 60. Gentamicin and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 61. Gentamicin and entecavir may increase each other's effects by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 62. Gentamicin decreases the levels of cyanocobalamin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown.
